defect.description: The edge case where new_mobject is old_mobject: the new deduplication removes the object from the list before searching, so scene.replace(a, a) no longer finds a, raises ValueError and leaves a removed from the scene; the deduplication must skip the case new_m is old_m (or run only after the replacement).
defect.location: src/scene.py (the deduplication at the top of replace_in_list)

review_items: Self-replace replace(A, A) broken: dedup removes A before search, raises ValueError
Destructive mutation: new_m removed before old_m found, scene corrupted on failure
Unconditional removal drops new_m from ancestor list when old_m is in a descendant list
list.remove drops only first occurrence; duplicates can remain
Design: move dedup inside the found branch
Pre-existing: only first occurrence of old_m replaced
votes.evidence_quote: `scene.replace(A, A)` where `A` is in the scene: line 38 removes `A` from the list, then the search on lines 42–45 finds nothing (it was just removed), returns `False`, and line 52 raises `ValueError("Could not find ...")`.
votes.justification: The review identifies the self-replace case at the dedup in replace_in_list. It explains that the dedup removes A before the search, so the search fails and ValueError is raised. This is the same defect and cause.
